title: Benchmark landing page layout + visual system for charts (incl. accessibility + disclaimers)
creator: Alicia Perez
description:
Goal
Design the public benchmark landing page + interactive results experience visual system so it is:
- Credible/technical (reads like an engineering benchmark, not a marketing page)
- Easy to scan and compare (tables + charts + tooltips)
- Accessible (WCAG 2.1 AA: contrast, focus, keyboard, reduced motion)
- Legally safe (clear comparative-language guardrails and visible disclaimers)

Context / scope
This ticket covers:
1) Landing page information architecture + layout grid (desktop/tablet/mobile)
2) Chart styling + patterns (bar/heatmap, p95 indicators, variance annotations)
3) Shared UI tokens for the benchmark experience (color, type scale, spacing, components)
4) Accessibility pass + requirements for implementation

Out of scope
- Data correctness (Applied ML owns)
- Copywriting (PMM/Content owns; we’ll provide layout guidance + callouts)
- Backend ingestion (Eng owns)

Primary stakeholders
- PMM/Launch: Soojin Lee
- Content: Ethan Wallace
- Web Eng: Felix Schneider
- Docs/Tech copy: Wei Chen
- Legal review partners: Michael Grant, Sofia Mendes
- Benchmark leads (for chart semantics/variance): Jonas Weber, Claire Dubois

Links
- Confluence web experience spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/benchmark-report-web-experience-spec.json
- Confluence interactive page requirements (PRD): sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/interactive-benchmark-page-requirements.json
- Linear: PM-826 (interactive requirements + analytics)

Deliverables
- Figma file with:
  - Layout: hero + key takeaways + interactive table section + methodology summary + FAQ + CTA modules
  - Responsive frames: 1440, 1024, 768, 375
  - Component specs: filter chips, dropdowns, metric toggle, tooltips, table cells, “Supported vs Experimental” badges, export controls
  - Chart patterns: latency/$ comparison (ranked bars), p95 heatmap, cost per 1M tokens, and “variance / stability” callouts
- Design tokens (light mode only for v1):
  - Chart palette with colorblind-safe ramps
  - Neutral palette for tables and gridlines
  - Focus ring + hover states
- Accessibility checklist for engineering implementation

IA / layout decisions (v1)
1) Hero section
- Title: “Production inference economics: latency per dollar” (PMM-approved phrasing)
- Subhead: Clarifies this is a Redwood-run benchmark; points to methodology + configs.
- Primary CTA: “View results” (scroll to interactive section)
- Secondary CTA: “Download PDF”
- Tertiary link: “How we measured” (methodology anchor)

2) Above-the-fold credibility block
- “What this benchmark is / is not” callout card to avoid over-claiming.
- Quick facts row (chips): Regions tested, run date range, workload mix summary, caching policy summary.

3) Interactive results section (core)
- Sticky filter rail on desktop; collapsible drawer on mobile.
- Table first (for exact values), chart view toggle optional (for scanning).
- Default view: latency/$ (p50 + p95 visible via hover or column toggle).
- Disclaimers and footnotes always visible near the controls (not hidden behind an info icon).

4) Methodology summary (non-negotiable)
- Short narrative + link to full methodology.
- “Key knobs” list (context length, concurrency, warmup, retries, caching/batching policy).
- “Stability” section with how we handle variance / reruns.

5) FAQ + CTA modules
- FAQ answers avoid comparative absolutes.
- CTA segmentation module:
  - Hosted: “Start with API credits”
  - Dedicated: “Get sizing help”
  - Private/VPC: “Talk to sales”

Chart visual system
- Principle: Use restrained, documentation-style visuals. Avoid gradient-heavy marketing styles.
- Bar charts (ranked):
  - One accent color for Redwood results; neutral color for “baseline/other” only if Legal approves the specific framing.
  - Numeric labels on bars for top 5; the rest via hover to reduce noise.
- Heatmaps:
  - Color ramp chosen for colorblind safety; do not rely on red/green contrast.
  - Always pair color with explicit numeric values or an accessible legend.
- Variance indicators:
  - “Stability badge” at row level: Stable / Needs re-run / Limited data (wording reviewed with Applied ML).
  - p95 volatility shown with a subtle sparkline or ± range in tooltip (no jitter animations).

Accessibility requirements (implementation notes)
- Minimum contrast:
  - Body text 4.5:1; non-text UI components 3:1.
  - Gridlines are decorative; do not convey meaning solely by thin low-contrast lines.
- Keyboard:
  - All filters, toggles, table sorting, and export are keyboard reachable.
  - Visible focus ring (2px) with offset; no focus suppression.
- Tooltips:
  - Must be accessible to keyboard and screen readers (ARIA-describedby). Avoid hover-only disclosure for key caveats.
- Reduced motion:
  - Respect prefers-reduced-motion: disable animated chart transitions.
- Responsive:
  - Mobile: table columns become selectable; show 2–3 key metrics with a “Change columns” control.

Open questions (resolved in comments below)
- Where to place disclaimers so Legal is satisfied without destroying UX?
- Should “Supported vs Experimental” be shown at model level, region level, or both?
- Whether to allow an explicit competitor toggle on v1 (strong Legal sensitivity)

Acceptance criteria
- Layout supports all required sections and matches the spec’s IA.
- Charts use the approved palette, legend pattern, and typography.
- Disclaimers are present in the interactive section and above-the-fold credibility block.
- Keyboard + focus states are explicitly designed for filters/table/tooltips.
- Mobile experience remains usable (no horizontal scrolling as the primary mechanism).
- Handoff includes specs usable by Felix (CSS tokens, spacing, component states).
comments: 2025-06-06 (Soojin Lee): Push for a more technical hero. Less “campaign-y.” Make “How we measured” prominent and ensure we don’t imply universal superiority. Prefer “latency per dollar” over “best value.”
2025-06-07 (Ethan Wallace): Request room for 3 key takeaways above the interactive table (short bullets + links to methodology). Also needs a clear path to the PDF download without hunting.
2025-06-10 (Jonas Weber): Heatmap must show exact numbers on cell focus/hover; color alone is misleading. Also add a visible note on run date range + hardware class equivalence assumptions (if any).

2025-06-11 (Felix Schneider): Implementation constraint: keep chart components simple (SVG + lightweight tooltip). Avoid heavy client-side chart libraries. Sticky filter rail is ok on desktop; mobile should be an overlay drawer.

2025-06-12 (Wei Chen): Accessibility: ensure disclaimers aren’t only in tooltips; needs inline text that can be indexed and translated later. Also: make sure anchor links don’t get hidden behind the sticky header.

2025-06-18 (Michael Grant): Disclaimers must be ‘clear and proximate’ to the results. Avoid superlatives and avoid phrases like “#1” or “industry-leading” unless tightly scoped and substantiated. If competitor context exists, it must be framed as “illustrative baseline” with sourcing and caveats.

2025-06-19 (Sofia Mendes): Prefer “Results will vary by workload” language. Make sure any comparison language is conditional (e.g., “in these workloads / under these settings”). Also request a consistent footnote style (a, b, c) rather than scattered asterisks.

2025-06-20 (Alicia Perez): Iteration 2 posted in Figma: moved “What this is / isn’t” into a small card under hero; added fixed disclaimer strip above table controls; reduced accent color saturation for charts for WCAG contrast. Added explicit focus states for chip filters + table headers.

2025-06-22 (Claire Dubois): Add a ‘Stability’ explanation block near the table: how many runs, rerun thresholds, and how we treat outliers. Also consider a label for results with limited region capacity windows.

2025-06-24 (Soojin Lee): Approves iteration 2. Request: keep above-the-fold minimal; put the 3 takeaways below fold but above interactive table. Also ensure the primary CTA scrolls to results, not PDF.

2025-06-26 (Felix Schneider): Handoff looks implementable. Notes: define max table row height; define truncation + expand behavior for model names; include empty-state design for filtered results. Please add specs for ‘export CSV/JSON’ buttons and loading states.

2025-06-27 (Alicia Perez): Iteration 3: added empty state, loading skeleton, and export control states (default/hover/focus/disabled). Confirmed mobile pattern: summary cards + column picker to avoid sideways scroll as primary path.
2025-06-28 (Michael Grant): Final design OK pending copy review; placement of disclaimers near controls is sufficient. Ensure there’s no ‘competitor toggle’ in v1 unless claims packet is approved.
2025-07-02 (Alicia Perez): Marking done for design. Follow-ups tracked in DES-961 for filter UX refinements + mobile column picker ergonomics.
activity_log: 2025-06-05: Ticket created; aligned scope with PM-826 and web experience spec.
2025-06-27: Final iteration + engineering handoff notes shared with Felix.
2025-07-12: Post-launch polish notes captured; follow-ups routed to DES-961.
engineering_handoff_notes: Use a single accent color for Redwood series; avoid multiple bright category colors.
Tooltip pattern: on focus/enter; close on escape; don’t trap focus.
Disclaimers: render as normal text in DOM (not canvas) and keep within same viewport as interactive controls.
Mobile: default to ‘Top metrics’ and allow column switcher; keep table sorting accessible.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion by disabling animated transitions in charts.
qa_checklist: Contrast checks on chart colors (including small text over fills).
Keyboard-only navigation through filters, table sort, and export controls.
Screen reader pass: headings, landmarks, aria labels for toggles and tooltips.
Responsive checks at 375/768/1024/1440; no critical content hidden behind sticky header.
Empty state + loading state + error state are styled and readable.
